# Recordings of the old console for console/mail/smtpwire

The files below are fixed records of what the real nodemailer of the Node
console did on the wire, made while the console still existed. They can't
be recorded again. The Go tests replay them and need no Node. Don't edit
them: when a fix changes a result on purpose, the test lists that
scenario as an intended difference with the row id.

| File | What it holds | Replayed by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sessions.json` | SMTP sessions of nodemailer against a scripted server | `TestSessions` (`sessions_test.go`), `TestRequireTLSOnTheRecordedDowngrades` |
| `vectors.json` | what single parts of nodemailer (and Node's certificate name check) answered for many inputs | the `Test...Vectors` tests and `TestCertificateNames` (`vectors_test.go`) |
| `e2e_sessions.json` | calls of the real `services/emailService.js` against a scripted server | `TestEndToEnd` (`e2e_test.go`) |

No mail left a recording. Every session went to a scripted server on
127.0.0.1. The Go tests have the same server (`sink_test.go`) and play the
same scripts.

The certificates in `certs` were made once by `gencerts`, and the
recordings were made with them. Don't make them again; `gencerts` may only
add new ones. The client trusted `certs/trusted.pem` through
`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, because the transport was created exactly as
`services/emailService.js` created it and so had no option for extra root
certificates.

## The scripted server

A script, as the `server` member of a session holds it:

- `tls`: true for implicit TLS (the handshake comes before the greeting)
- `cert`: name of the key and chain under `certs`
- `greeting`: ops run when a client has connected
- `rules`: `{ VERB: [ops, ops, ...] }`; the nth line with that verb runs
  the nth list, the last list repeats. No rule: `250 OK`.

Verbs: the first word of a command line in upper case (`MAIL`, `RCPT`),
`AUTH <MECHANISM>` for AUTH (falls back to the rule `AUTH`), the name given
by an op `{cont: name}` for the line after it, `ENDDATA` when the message
data is complete, `DOT` for a line with a single dot, `EMPTY` for an empty
line.

Ops: `{w: text}` write (text holds bytes as Latin-1 characters),
`{wrep: {s, n}}` write s n times, `{sleep: ms}`, `{tls: 1}` start TLS,
`{data: 1}` read message data next, `{cont: name}` read the next line as
verb name, `{close: 1}` close the sending side, `{stall: 1}` never answer
again.

Recorded events of the client's side: `{e:'tls', sni}`, `{e:'tlsfail'}`,
`{e:'line', s}`, `{e:'data', b64}` or `{e:'data', len, sha256}` for large
data, `{e:'partial', s}` for bytes without a line end before the client
closed, `{e:'eof'}` when the client closed.

## sessions.json

A list of scenarios, one per line:

- `name`, `call` (`send` or `verify`)
- `hostname`: what `os.hostname()` returned (`{value}`) or that it threw
  (`{error: true}`)
- `options`: `host`, `port` (the port the server listened on, 0 for
  nodemailer's default), `secure`, `user`, `pass`, `tlsVerify` and the
  timeouts in ms
- `envelope`: the envelope `smtp-connection` was given (after mime-node,
  or the one a scenario forced in), `message`: `{s}` bytes as Latin-1
  characters or `{gen: {seed, size, alphabet}}` for generated bytes
- `dns`: the A (`a`) and AAAA (`aaaa`) records the recording gave the host
  of the scenario; without it the lookups were those of the machine
- `server`: the script, `{listen: false}` when nothing listened
- `client`: the recorded events of the client's side
- `outcome`: `{ok: true}`, `{info: {...}}` or
  `{error: {message, code, response, responseCode, command, ...}}`
- `cmp`: what a replay does not compare, with the reason in the comment of
  `TestSessions`

## e2e_sessions.json

Made by calling `sendEmail`, `sendAlertEmail`, `sendHelpRequestEmail` and
`testConnection` of the real `services/emailService.js`. Its database
adapter was replaced by a stub whose `getSetting('smtp_config')` returned
the session's setting; everything else was the real code, with the
environment in `env` (no `SMTP_*`, `PANEL_PUBLIC_URL` or `PUBLIC_URL`
variables).

Top level: `nodemailer` (version), `env`, `panelBaseUrl` (what
`getPanelBaseUrl()` returned), `sessions`. Each session:

- `name`
- `hostname`: the machine name during the call (`console.example.test`)
- `config`: the value `getSetting('smtp_config')` returned: a JSON string,
  an object for the sessions stored as object, `null` for no setting. Its
  `port` is `port`, the port the server listened on (a closed port when
  `server` is `null`); a replay puts its own port there.
- `call`: `{fn, args}`, the function and its arguments
- `result`: what the function returned (`true`, `false`, `{success}` or
  `{success, error}`). An error text can hold the port as a number
  (`connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:45109`).
- `logs`: the console lines of the call, `{level, text}`, with the port
  replaced by `{port}`
- `server`: the script (`null`: nothing listened)
- `client`: the client's side of the session: `{e: "line", s}` for every
  command line (bytes as Latin-1 characters), `{e: "tls", sni}` where TLS
  started, `{e: "data", b64}` for the bytes after DATA up to and including
  the end line (base64, always in full here), `{e: "eof"}` when the client
  closed. No events: the call made no connection.

The DATA bytes hold what nodemailer generated for that call: a Message-ID,
a Date and MIME boundaries that differed on every run.
